exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies at greater than 24 + 0 weeks gestation with live birth and clinically-diagnosed chorioamnionitis between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2021.
finding: The rate of early onset neonatal sepsis and maternal infectious morbidity was greater in the cesarean section group compared to vaginal delivery, with neonatal sepsis being particularly high in those with abnormal fetal surveillance.
mod_finding: The rate of early onset neonatal sepsis was highest in the cesarean section group, particularly in those with abnormal fetal surveillance, and maternal infectious morbidity was also greater with cesarean section.
